title: Microsoft and Chevron Sign 20-Year Power Deal For Texas Data Center
key_facts: A project by Chevron and Engine No. 1 secured a 20-year agreement to supply natural-gas electricity to a Microsoft data center in West Texas.
The 2.67-gigawatt power plant is called Project Kilby and will sit alongside the data center.
Partners expect a final investment decision this year and generation from 2028.
Most capacity comes from GE Vernova turbines; the rest from Caterpillar's Solar Turbines.
Chevron says power is not designed to flow through the existing grid at first, to limit the effect on consumers' prices.
quote_evidence: A project by Chevron Corp and Engine No. 1 has secured an agreement to supply natural gas-based electricity to a Microsoft data center project in West Texas for 20 years.
The partners expect to make a final investment decision this year and start generation from the project in 2028.
why_it_matters_hint: A single gas plant dedicated to one tech company's data center, with no grid link at first.
